x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 reported that WALR on fresh rupee loans fell by 64 basis points in FY26, which it called robust pass-through. Some notes give 69 bps instead, but 64 bps is the figure in the notes. 125 bps was the cumulative repo cut since February 2025, not the fall in WALR.

The High Denomination Bank Notes (Demonetisation) Act, 1978, under Morarji Desai, demonetised the ₹1,000, ₹5,000 and ₹10,000 notes to curb black money. Option B (₹500, ₹1,000, ₹10,000) is how one source (APP) lists it, and option D is the 1946 episode.

All four are correct per the Economic Survey 2025-26. Over FY26 the repo rate was cut by 100 bps to 5.25% (the cumulative cut since February 2025, from 6.50%, is 125 bps). The CRR was cut by 100 bps to 3%. OMO purchases were ₹2.39 lakh crore in April-May 2025 and ₹1 lakh crore in December 2025.

Heavy government borrowing is an obstacle because it keeps yields high (crowding out). A permanent end to government borrowing is neither listed nor real, so B is the answer. Structural rigidities in banking, liquidity mismatches, and cash preference with a large unorganised money market are all listed obstacles to transmission.
